```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(cli.num_colors = 1, width = 80)
set.seed(1)
```

```{r setup}
library(yourhonor)
```

Calibration compares a judge with humans on the items you have. A bias probe
asks a different question: does the judge's label move when the input changes
in a way that should not matter? This article probes the synthetic judge from
`vignette("yourhonor")`, whose planted flaw is that any input longer than 240
characters is graded one level more generously. No input in `synthetic_gold`
is that long, so calibration could not see the flaw.

```{r}
keyword_judge <- function(data) {
  hedged <- grepl("probably|somewhere|should be|I think|I believe|might|sometimes|could", data$input)
  concrete <- grepl("Answer: (Open|Use|Yes)|click", data$input)
  label <- ifelse(hedged, "P", ifelse(concrete, "C", "I"))
  # The flaw under audit: a long input reads as one level more complete.
  long <- nchar(data$input) > 240
  label[long & label == "P"] <- "C"
  label[long & label == "I"] <- "P"
  # A little run-to-run error, so repeated runs are not identical.
  noise <- runif(nrow(data)) < 0.05
  label[noise] <- sample(c("I", "P", "C"), sum(noise), replace = TRUE)
  tibble::tibble(.item_id = data$.item_id, label = label)
}
```

## Probe pointwise bias

Pointwise probes score control and treatment rows in one randomized batch.
The verbosity probe pads each answer with filler; the self-preference and
bandwagon probes prepend a short framing sentence. `no_signal` means no
directional effect was detected by that probe; it is not a claim that bias is
absent.

```{r}
bias <- probe_bias(
  synthetic_gold,
  keyword_judge,
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  probes = c("verbosity", "self_preference", "bandwagon"),
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
bias[, c("probe", "directional_rate", "direction", "p_value_adj", "verdict")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# "\x60" is a backtick: inline code cannot contain one literally.
code <- function(x) paste0("\x60", x, "\x60")
verdict_of <- function(probe) code(bias$verdict[bias$probe == probe])
# "both `no_signal`" when the two verdicts agree, "`a` and `b`" otherwise.
verdicts_of <- function(probes) {
  verdicts <- bias$verdict[match(probes, bias$probe)]
  if (length(unique(verdicts)) == 1L) paste("both", code(verdicts[1])) else paste(code(verdicts), collapse = " and ")
}
```

The padded answers cross the judge's 240-character threshold, so the
verbosity probe's verdict is `r verdict_of("verbosity")`: labels move towards
the perturbed (longer) version. The short framing prefixes do not cross it,
so the self-preference and bandwagon probes report
`r verdicts_of(c("self_preference", "bandwagon"))`. A `BIAS`
verdict needs both a small adjusted p-value and a `directional_rate` above
`flip_threshold`. `flip_rate` counts a label change in either direction and
`directional_rate` only the net movement one way, so a large but balanced
`flip_rate` is reported but never flagged:

```{r}
bias[, c("probe", "flip_rate", "directional_rate", "verdict")]
```

## Missing and unscored items

Missingness is reported on two denominators. `missing_rate` is the share of
individual judgments that came back `NA` and is gated directly;
`unscored_rate` is the share of items that could not be scored, which for the
position probe also includes within-condition ties. A policy's upper bounds
count every unscored item against the judge, over all supplied items: as a
flip in the flip-rate bound, and as a flip in whichever single direction gives
the larger bound in the directional one. Its lower bounds, which a `FAIL` must
clear, resolve in the judge's favour the unscored items that a completion of
their missing judgments could score: as unflipped in the flip-rate bound,
and in the way that most cancels the observed direction in the directional
one. Items lost to a within-condition tie no answer could break
(`n_unscored_tied`: a display order judged in every repeat whose choices
tie) are decided evidence, not missing, so they stay out of the lower
bounds. Abstention can therefore keep a probe from passing, but cannot fail
it through the items it leaves unscored. (With `repeats >= 2` a position
item can stay scored with some repeats missing; its modal choice is taken as
observed in both bounds, so those missing repeats can still cause a `FAIL`
or, within the missing-rate tolerance, turn a deserved `FAIL` into a
`PASS`.)

```{r}
bias[, c("probe", "n_scored", "n_unscored", "unscored_rate", "missing_rate")]
```

`?probe_bias` documents every column and its denominator.

## Probe position bias

Position bias uses a separate structured API for a *pairwise* judge. Source
columns are swapped and shown to the judge only as neutral `.candidate_1` and
`.candidate_2` slots, then display choices are mapped back to stable candidate
identity. A pairwise judge is a different instrument from the pointwise judge
audited above, so it gets its own `audit_id`.

```{r}
pairs <- tibble::tibble(
  question = c("2 + 2?", "Capital of France?"),
  candidate_a = c("4", "Paris"),
  candidate_b = c("5", "Berlin")
)
always_first <- function(data) rep("A", nrow(data))
position <- probe_position(
  pairs,
  always_first,
  candidate_a_col = "candidate_a",
  candidate_b_col = "candidate_b",
  context_cols = "question",
  repeats = 2,
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "pairwise-judge-v1"
)
position[, c("probe", "flip_rate", "position_preference", "direction", "verdict")]
```

Every item flipped with the display order and the preference is entirely for
the first slot, yet the verdict is `r code(position$verdict)`: `r nrow(pairs)` items
cannot reach significance in a sign test. A real position audit needs a
proper item count, which is what `min_probe_n` in a policy enforces.

## Evidence for one judge only

Because its `audit_id` differs, `report()` refuses to bind the position
evidence to a calibration of the pointwise judge rather than silently
assessing two judges as one:

```{r, error = TRUE}
cal <- calibrate_judge(
  synthetic_gold,
  judge = keyword_judge,
  human_cols = c("rater_1", "rater_2", "rater_3"),
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  id_col = "id",
  label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
  scale = "ordinal",
  n_boot = 500,
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
report(cal, bias = position)
```

The pointwise probes share the calibration's `audit_id`, so
`report(cal, bias = bias)` binds them; `vignette("policies-audit")` gates
them with a policy.
